decisions.evidence: Skeptic is right: revert to game. The assigner's boundary note claims the player_* seeds are 'Chimera hook labels' - they are not; symbols/opensauce.txt gives them at exact entry points (0x47b140 player_examine_nearby_vehicle, 0x47b940 player_set_action_result, 0x47bb30 player_set_action_result_to_network, 0x47bf23 player_handle_action..., 0x47c250 player_over_shield_screen_effect, 0x47c310 player_camo_screen_effect, 0x47c3d0 player_health_pack_screen_effect) and symbols/candidates_cea.json maps player_examine_nearby_vehicle / player_set_action_result / player_health_pack_screen_effect to module 'game'. Structurally decisive: OpenSauce also puts players.c jump tables and hooks INSIDE this span - 0x47afe2/0x47afe8/0x47b008/0x47b014 player_examine_nearby_objects_server/client_jmp_table, 0x47bf28/0x47bf39/0x47c21b/0x47c228 player_handle_action_jmp_table - so 0x47b140-0x47c3ef is the tail of the uninterrupted player_* run that starts at 0x474c00 (player_control_get_unit_camera_info, 0x477970 player_index_from_unit_index, 0x478820 player_teleport, 0x47aac1 player_spawn__create_unit_mp_hook). The real hs-external object file does not start until ~0x47c400: every stub from 0x47cf09 (hs_function_table_reference_0) onward carries an hs_function_table reference, and there is NOT ONE such reference anywhere in 0x47b140-0x47c3ef. The calls to hs_return (0x48a640) / hs arg-stack (0x48a850) only mean these players.c routines are script-callable - 0x48a850 has exactly three callers and all three are these player functions, i.e. this is players.c's own hs glue, not the hs library's. pack.py confirms subject matter: 0x47b140 walks the player array via DAT_008603b0+0x34 (stride 0xc) and toggles object+0x107 bit 0; 0x47b940 uses PTR_DAT_00688b58[player] and sets object+0x106 bit 5; 0x47c3d0 just forwards to 0x4f6ec0. Applies to all five: 0x47b140, 0x47b940, 0x47bf23, 0x47c310, 0x47c3d0. The run boundary belongs at ~0x47c400, not 0x47b140.

Skeptic is wrong here: keep hs. MSVC contiguity cuts against the proposal rather than for it - the sv_* implementations the skeptic points at all live in one object file at 0x4e2ed0-0x4e4b50 (slice 08, networking, e.g. 0x4e4b50 prints "sv_rcon_password: '%s'"). A source file cannot be split across 0x482xxx and 0x4e2xxx, so these 13 stubs are provably NOT in the server-console source file; they are in whatever file occupies 0x482b20-0x4830b0. That file is the hs external-function table file: OpenSauce marks an hs_function_table reference inside essentially every stub in a dense unbroken band from 0x47cf09 to ~0x485xxx, including 0x482b38 (inside 0x482b20), 0x482b88 (inside 0x482b70), 0x482d18, 0x482da9, 0x482f08, 0x482f78, 0x482fe8, 0x483048 (inside 0x483010), 0x4830a8 (inside 0x483060), and continuing straight into 0x483108/0x483168 - i.e. there is no object-file seam at 0x4830b0/0x483100; the sv_* stubs are just entries 227-240 of the same ~355-entry stub run that also contains hs_null_with_params_evaluate (0x483430) and hs_null_evaluate (0x483f40). pack.py confirms the stubs are pure hs plumbing with zero server logic: local_4/local_8 zeroed, FUN_0048ad60(param_2,param_3,&local_4,&local_8) parses the script args, then one tail call to the networking routine plus hs_return (0x48a640). Being the script/console entry point for a networking command does not move the code into networking's object file. Applies to the whole run 0x482b20-0x4830b0 (0x482b20, 0x482b70, 0x482cb0, 0x482d00, 0x482d50, 0x482da0, 0x482ed0, 0x482f20, 0x482f70, 0x482fc0, 0x483010, 0x483060, 0x4830b0).
